boundary when semantic behaviour stays the same; and simplifying proof
fixtures or module-derived tests without changing their governing module
claims. Examples that are not opportunistic clean-up and therefore require
explicit design re-entry include repricing lookup, indexing, caching or
persistence strategy across module boundaries; changing public carriers,
visibility or ownership of truth; widening effect boundaries or runtime
observability doctrine; and introducing performance behaviour that changes
product expectations rather than only improving local realisation quality
(P6).

A cross-boundary opportunity discovered during lawful clean-up is not
silently absorbed into the active boundary; it is repricing input. If the
owning authority admits follow-up implementation, that work enters
separately at the smallest lawful re-entry point (SPEC_METHOD §4). This
profile owns the scope-separation rule, not the work-tracking mechanism;
for ticketed work, TICKETS governs whether admitted follow-up is recorded
and how it affects ticket closure (P6). The test: if the improvement stays
inside the active boundary and preserves declared behaviour, it is lawful
clean-up; if it changes authority, public meaning or cross-boundary
realisation doctrine, it is a new design decision. Leaving an opened area
better than it was found is good realisation practice; using clean-up as
cover for unauthorised redesign is not (P2, P6).

### Recurrence extraction

When the same realisation pattern appears across more than one processed
boundary, review treats that pattern as a commonisation candidate rather
than as another purely local clean-up (P2, P4a). Module boundaries make this review
possible: they constrain computation and evaluation enough that repeated
local shapes can be compared honestly and consolidated into libraries
without changing product truth. A recurrence candidate is usually not
product truth, authority-neutral, reused across two or more tickets or
module boundaries, and consumable through local adapters without changing
semantic ownership. Typical candidates include expectation derivation;
nested contract or policy carriers; proof-helper or fixture shaping;
effect-edge request or plan shaping; and constructor or materialisation
helpers that do not own semantic law.

The rule of two, its third-rebuild threshold and the commonisation order
are owned by
[TICKETS §6 Recurring realisation and library declaration](TICKETS.md#recurring-realisation-and-library-declaration),
which applies them to every implementation migration ticket together with
the fields `library_usage`, `governing_library` and `library_rationale`.
This profile refines that rule for design review: a third local rebuild
is not design-method conformant unless the active boundary consumes an
existing reusable library or commonisation surface, extends that surface
before the local implementation lands, or review records an explicit
do-not-commonise decision and why the pattern is still boundary-specific
(P2). This section defines the design review obligation, not a rival
ticket rule or lifecycle (P6).

Under the commonisation order that TICKETS §6 owns, if a reusable
pattern remains tenant-local and authority-neutral, it should be extracted into a reusable
library or common realisation surface rather than recreated inside each
module. If commonisation would change ownership, public carriers, module
boundaries or shared common law, it is no longer recurrence extraction; it
is a separate design decision and is treated that way (P6). Commonisation
closes only when the selected path consumes the accepted relation and the
superseded production responsibility is retired or satisfies the retention
relation of SPEC_METHOD §7 Closure criterion. Compare removed work and
maintained responsibilities across the path; shared names, fewer lines or
an unused common helper do not establish contraction (P2, P4b).

### Post-ticket design review

When a ticket applies this profile to its boundary and claims that
boundary has been processed, the design-method closure claim should not rest on
implementation status alone (P6, P2). The processed boundary is checked
against its accepted design basis and exact closure claim before the
ticket claims closure under this profile. The check may be part of the
ticket's normal verification; it does not require a separate artifact,
review round or reviewer. TICKETS remains the authority for ticket status,
closure mechanics, reopening, dependency handling and follow-up ticket
recording; this rule states what the design check covers when this
profile governs the ticketed boundary.

The check determines whether the boundary stayed lawful under the current
design and module assets; whether the exact claim includes every causally
applicable live requirement, accepted design relation and retained
predecessor claim; whether the exact closure claim leaves competing or
ambiguous authority on its acceptance path; whether implementation
established a material architectural decision with durable consequences
that forecloses an admitted Product outcome; and whether any discovered
issue falsifies the current claim or an applicable hard stop (P6, P4b).

The check reconstructs the complete selected function from governing
requirements through the accepted Ontology, Prime atoms, IACS, views,
target modules, implementation and module-owned proof; it does not begin
and end with the previous review findings. Exact hashes establish subject
identity; headings and artifact presence establish location; green tests
establish only the properties they actually assert. None supplies a
missing semantic relation or substitutes a weaker property for the
governed claim (P6; EVALUATION §1).

The complete selected function is the causal closure of the declared
claim, not the whole Product or the whole history of its construction. The
unchanged-boundary rules of §5 and §7 permit reuse of a current accepted
Ontology, design verdict and sufficient reconstruction evidence as closed
results under [ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse),
which owns reuse and its three invalidators: the check confirms their
exact scope, traces and applicability, and that none of those invalidators
has occurred. The invalidators those rules name are instances of
ACTIVATION §7's three, and no fourth exists: a reprice of a governing
source, which invalidates only the affected Ontology relations and
downstream projections until their impact is re-evaluated (§5), is a
changed basis for those relations and projections; a later candidate
that satisfies the applicability criteria and could materially alter the
lawful frontier (§7) is a material input change for the affected
selection evidence; new evidence or another material dimension that
defeats a dominance relation (§7) is a material input change for that
relation. A new role, conversation or review occurrence is not one of
them, so it does not itself require re-authoring that evidence or
recreating the three views. Missing, stale or ambiguous coverage is not a
no-delta proof. A material changed relation or a new counterexample is an
instance of that section's material input change: it requires affected
reconstruction and the applicable design gate, conserving supported
unaffected relations. This reuse does not weaken §7's complete Ontology
and three-view coverage for a new or materially changed boundary (P2, P6).

The required consequence: an issue that falsifies the current claim or an
applicable hard stop blocks the design-method closure claim, because that
claim is then `falsified`, which never becomes `satisfied`
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)), and a hard stop is not
waived ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)). Whether
a finding also blocks the boundary's current promotion is decided by
[EVALUATION §5 When a finding blocks promotion](EVALUATION.md#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion).
The check's determinations above are this profile's domain triggers for
that section's four conditions: a discovered falsifying issue for the
first; competing or ambiguous authority on the acceptance path for the
second; a boundary that is not lawful under the current design and module
assets, or a claim that omits a causally applicable requirement, accepted design
relation or retained predecessor claim, for the third; and the durable
architectural foreclosure for the fourth. Applied to this check: ticket or
review wording cannot narrow applicable active authority away;
boundary-local clean-up or commonisation is absorbed only when required to
make the current claim true, preserve singular authority, satisfy accepted
design, or avoid the durable architectural foreclosure above; other
clean-up, recurrence, generality and cross-boundary opportunities are
observations outside the exact claim, which EVALUATION §5 returns as
repricing inputs that do not automatically widen the subject, block its
bounded claim or require a follow-up ticket; and any repricing admitted by
the owning authority enters through the smallest lawful re-entry point
(SPEC_METHOD §4) (P6, P2). The rule keeps design closure truthful without turning discovery
into automatic scope expansion: current defects and hard stops remain
blocking, useful observations may survive as repricing input, and
unclaimed future capability and optional clean-up do not become implicit
work. No processed ticket that applies this profile should claim
design-method closure until this bounded design check is complete.

### Interface bleed prohibition

No interface should bleed semantic authority into another interface family
(P6). Interface bleed exists when one
interface reconstructs another interface's source truth; projection logic
becomes closure logic; report or prompt logic becomes admission logic;
public wrappers decide kernel semantics; or adapters invent meaning instead
of translating boundaries. The required shape: each interface family has
one authoritative source truth; downstream interfaces consume that truth;
crossing an interface boundary does not create a new semantic centre. Low
coupling requires semantic non-bleed, not only small functions.

### Proxy interface prohibition

Projects using this profile do not use proxy or partial interface
implementation as a substitute for real migration or real design
completion (P6; SPEC_METHOD §7
Bridge prohibition). A proxy interface is a new-looking surface that
forwards to the old authority path, reconstructs missing truth from the
old path, keeps the old path executable behind a new name, or allows
proofs to stay green while the old law still governs. This is bridge debt,
not progress. If compatibility is intentionally retained, it is treated as
an explicit feature with its own bounded authority and proof; otherwise
the proxy path is removed.

## 11. Review

Prompts under this profile follow
[ACTIVATION §2](ACTIVATION.md#2-context-construction-under-an-envelope),
prompt construction. A worker may be told where to inspect and what
contract to satisfy. A prompt clause that exists to enforce design law
needs provenance and a proof that the clause still causes or prevents the
intended behaviour (P6, P1).

### Design review questions

When reviewing code under this profile, ask (P6):

1. Does semantic law live in typed carriers or in orchestration code?
2. Are the main steps readable as transforms over admitted truth?
3. Are effects isolated to explicit edge modules?
4. Can projections or reports invent closure independently?
5. Does each projection or query module derive from an admitted source
   carrier, or can it reconstruct a same-name but structurally different
   truth surface?
6. Is mutation justified, bounded and local?
7. Can consumers pattern-match the source carrier directly?
8. Is any proxy or compatibility surface still silently authoritative?
9. Would removing the authoritative carrier make the system fail closed
   rather than silently rebuilding truth?
10. Does each new function project accepted Prime atoms without
    convenience aggregation or rival semantic authority?
11. Does any interface bleed semantic authority into another interface
    family?
12. For Python, does any governed semantic surface still rely on `Any`,
    open dictionary payloads or untyped definitions?
13. Has the boundary declared its IACS?
14. Which shapes are Subordinate Payloads, and why are they not staying
    subordinate?
15. Does every promoted top-level type pass the Promotion Test?
16. Has typed closure caused Boundary Inflation by multiplying peer types
    or parallel schema migrations?
17. Does this change avoid increasing truth surfaces, and reduce duplicate
    truth where duplicate truth exists?
18. Is any foreign or open payload still trusted past ingress?
19. Did enforcement follow proof, or is the typing or schema work
    cosmetic?
20. If this boundary governs another actor, is it publishing state and
    admissible routes, or imperatively prescribing strategy?
21. If a reference realisation exists, has the target boundary been
    derived explicitly from reference design to target design to target
    module assets rather than from code drift?
22. Does a module-bounded domain projection exist and accurately show IACS
    carriers, their Prime-atom projection mappings, subordinate payloads,
    visibility, ownership and deferred families from the accepted
    Ontology?
23. Do the unit tests derive from module ownership and module assets
    rather than from helper layout or incidental code shape?
24. If the change claims clean-up or optimisation, does it stay
    boundary-local, behaviour-preserving and authority-neutral rather than
    becoming silent redesign?
25. If a cross-boundary opportunity was discovered, was it kept out of the
    current change unless the owning authority admitted it at the lawful
    re-entry point?
26. If the same realisation pattern has already appeared elsewhere, did
    review make an explicit library or commonisation decision rather than
    allowing another silent local rebuild?
27. If this would be the third local rebuild of the same realisation
    pattern, is the change design-method conformant because it consumes or
    extends the governing library or records an explicit do-not-commonise
    decision?
28. If the ticket is making a design-method closure claim, did the bounded
    design check cover the exact claim and applicable hard stops without
    automatically absorbing optional discovery?
29. If the project is governed by the graph-execution profile, is this
    module realising a declared outcome traversal rather than substituting
    for the graph function?
30. Has review checked whether a deterministic module boundary is actually
    an operative edge traversal that should be declared under the
    graph-execution profile?
31. Do `F_D` uses establish the common total-domain contract and retain their
    operation profiles, and do evaluators, deterministic transforms and effect shells remain
    subordinate to the GTL and ABG graph carrier rather than becoming the
    hidden program?
32. Does the boundary have a lifecycle confirmation against the canonical
    operational lifecycle chain of SPEC_METHOD §2, or named `Gap:` or
    `Unanswered:` items for unresolved phases?
33. Are release, deployment, live usage, observed telemetry and retirement
    questions answered by the proper authority surface rather than invented
    by implementation, prompt prose, local convention or fixtures?
34. If a lifecycle phase is declared not applicable, is the reason explicit
    and compatible with the product and requirement authority?
35. Does the boundary have distinct Mermaid domain, sequence and
    state-machine views rather than one carrier inventory or broad
    flowchart?
36. Does every sequence participant exist in the domain model, and does
    every message bind to a declared transform, graph or computation
    constructor, interpreter act or effect boundary?
37. Does every state transition derive from admitted carrier, event or
    projection truth rather than controller-local memory?
38. Does the axiom matrix evaluate every applicable product, graph,
    language, runtime, handler and module law with `pass`, `fail` or
    reasoned `not_applicable`?
39. Is any relied-on graph, batch, retry, recursion or workflow
    constructor still `semantic_not_realized`, and if so are promotion and
    closure blocked rather than bypassed with imperative glue?
40. Is the proportional sequencing relation justified, and is the design
    verdict explicitly `accepted` before promotion or closure and, where
    design-gated, before retained implementation establishes an unresolved
    or contradictory relation or chooses a materially non-equivalent
    network?
41. Does one accepted Ontology exist before IACS, public operation, schema,
    module or implementation promotion?
42. Does the Ontology enumerate entities, identities, relationships,
    invariants and logical lifecycle completeness without treating mutable
    CRUD as the default?
43. Does every Ontology function or transition declare proposer,
    evaluator, verifier, admitter, executor, projector and retirement
    authority as applicable, with actor and capability kept distinct from
    authority?
44. Has every discovered functionality item been derived through an atomic
    function or higher-order composition, explicitly deferred or excluded,
    or assigned to a named gap?
45. Was Prime contraction applied to the complete candidate semantic-atom
    family and all proposed realisation projections, with every accepted
    atom's admitted domain recorded, rather than only to functions,
    carriers or isolated units?
46. Does the boundary declare its composition and effect algebra and prove
    identity, closure, cardinality, effect and authority conservation where
    applicable?
47. Are the class, sequence, state, IACS, public contract, adapter, code
    and test surfaces traceable projections of the Ontology with any
    accepted loss declared?
48. Would removing the Ontology reveal ungrounded meaning in a downstream
    view, operation register, controller or implementation branch?
49. Before constructing a material generic capability or common mechanic,
    was it stated without Product, domain, module, vendor, file or
    incumbent labels, with declared semantic or authority-bearing
    relations distinguished from generic mechanics?
50. Does bounded discovery record every searched source or category,
    cutoff time and version basis, applicability criteria, exclusions,
    predecessor or incumbent status, and residual unknown, with later
    material candidates invalidating affected selection evidence?
51. Did foundation selection compare credible candidate compositions
    across the decision-relevant lifecycle dimensions without incumbent,
    source-order, local-code or dependency-count preference?
52. Are hard authority, Product-contract, safety, security, licensing and
    constructability failures eliminative, while unknown evidence remains
    explicit rather than becoming a favourable score?
53. Does every reused foundation hold only explicitly assigned roles,
    preserving each declared relation's owner, role kind, subject, scope,
    basis, lifecycle and refusal invariants without authority widening?
54. Is the selected composition undominated under the evidence, and did
    the existing trade-off owner apply declared priorities and risk
    tolerances rather than asserting an undefined total ordering?
55. Does every rejected material candidate carry decisive evidence or a
    falsifier, while an unresolved frontier remains a gap rather than an
    unsupported preference?
56. Did any newly exposed material generic subproblem recursively re-enter
    the foundation-selection relation before its implementation was
    retained?

An unanswered required relation withholds the conformance claim that
depends on it. Record the unanswered relation and the evidence needed to
decide it, then diagnose the gap at its actual owner under
[ACTIVATION §1 Feedback and diagnosis](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation).
A missing authority declaration or observation does not by itself show
excessive coupling or imperative design. That diagnosis requires evidence
that meaning is held in orchestration or outside the declared carriers
and transforms, under [SPEC_METHOD §2 Realisation shape](SPEC_METHOD.md#realisation-shape)
(P6, P2, P1).

### Functional realisation checklist

When a project claims functional bias, pure transforms, immutable
carriers, single-owner truth or low-coupling realisation, review
explicitly checks (P6, P5):

- [ ] the change preserves the constitutional WHAT and keeps realisation
      work inside lawful HOW surfaces only;
- [ ] the active boundary has one accepted Ontology that derives its
      entities, identities, relationships, invariants, lifecycle,
      authority, atomic functions, higher-order composition, effects and
      projections;
- [ ] the entity-lifecycle completeness matrix gives every declare/create,
      read/project, update/transition and delete/retire question a lawful
      function, reasoned `not_applicable` or named owned gap;
- [ ] the authority matrix distinguishes actor, capability, proposal,
      evaluation, verification, admission, execution, projection and
      retirement without implicit authority widening;
- [ ] the function-derivation matrix disposes every discovered
      functionality item and prevents direct verb-to-operation promotion;
- [ ] whole-family Prime contraction has factored repeated behaviour into
      parameterised atomic functions and declared higher-order
      composition before peer functions, operations or carriers are
      promoted;
- [ ] Prime evidence covers the complete candidate semantic-atom family,
      records every accepted atom's admitted domain, and maps accepted
      atoms to every proposed realisation projection;
- [ ] the IACS, three views, public contracts, adapters, implementation
      and tests are fidelity-checked projections of the accepted Ontology
      rather than independent design authorities;
- [ ] if a reference realisation exists, the new realisation is
      functionally equivalent at the semantic boundary without copying
      incidental implementation drift;
- [ ] if a reference realisation exists, the target design explicitly maps
      reference design to target design to target module boundary before
      implementation;
- [ ] before constructing a material generic capability, the boundary ran
      the proportional foundation-selection pass (UP-023, §5), recorded
      bounded discovery and the undominated frontier, distinguished
      declared relations from generic mechanics, preserved every assigned
      role and authority tuple, and recorded decisive evidence for
      selected and rejected candidates;
- [ ] implementation and unit tests both derive from the same module
      boundary assets rather than from code-first decomposition;
- [ ] each semantic truth surface still has one clear authoritative owner;
- [ ] the change reduces duplicated truth, controller reconstruction and
      rival local authority paths;
- [ ] semantic functions consume admitted carriers only;
- [ ] semantic functions are pure for the same admitted inputs;
- [ ] time, randomness, UUID minting, environment reads, process state,
      filesystem, network and global registries are absent from the
      semantic centre;
- [ ] if identity is introduced, identity creation is explicitly owned by
      a declared ingress or effect boundary rather than hidden inside
      semantic helpers;
- [ ] carriers are immutable and returned as new values rather than
      mutated in place;
- [ ] shared mutable state is absent from the semantic centre;
- [ ] semantic transforms operate directly on local admitted carriers
      rather than re-entering parsers, validators or loaders on locally
      assembled truth;
- [ ] invalid or incomplete truth is rejected at ingress instead of being
      repaired procedurally inside semantic code;
- [ ] defaults are explicit, ratified and carrier-owned rather than
      helper-owned;
- [ ] each function has one clear owner and one clear responsibility rather
      than mixing admission, semantics and effects;
- [ ] coupling is low by dependency shape: semantic algebra depends on
      carrier contracts, not runtime shells; admission depends on
      validation, not semantic orchestration; effect code stays at the
      edge;
- [ ] no function both decides semantic meaning and performs effects;
- [ ] effect boundaries are explicit, typed and unable to erase carrier
      truth into open objects;
- [ ] package, bootstrap, controller, adapter and runtime-shell layers stay
      below the semantic centre;
- [ ] governance and observability surfaces publish facts, eligibility and
      provenance only, without imperative builder or executor strategy;
- [ ] the active boundary has complete Mermaid domain, sequence and
      state-machine views that match the current IACS, visibility,
      ownership, behaviour, lifecycle and deferred-family split;
- [ ] the active boundary carries a complete cross-view axiom matrix and
      an explicit `accepted` design verdict with no bypassed realisation
      gap;
- [ ] the unit tests for the active boundary derive from module ownership,
      IACS and structural carrier assets rather than from helper layout;
- [ ] if the change includes clean-up or optimisation, it stays
      boundary-local, behaviour-preserving and authority-neutral;
- [ ] if the same realisation pattern has appeared before, the ticket has
      made an explicit library or commonisation decision rather than
      rebuilding it again silently;
- [ ] if a reusable library or commonisation surface exists, the ticket
      explicitly consumes or extends it rather than duplicating the
      pattern locally;
- [ ] if no reusable library or commonisation surface is used, there is an
      explicit rationale that the pattern is boundary-specific or not yet
      a lawful commonisation candidate;
- [ ] if a cross-boundary opportunity was discovered, it was kept out of
      the current change unless the owning authority admitted it at the
      lawful re-entry point;
- [ ] if the ticket is making a design-method closure claim, the bounded
      design check covered the exact claim and applicable hard stops
      without automatically absorbing optional discovery;
- [ ] a negative proof shows that an imperative bypass, open-payload
      bypass or effect-edge erasure fails closed;
- [ ] if the project is governed by the graph-execution profile, the
      deterministic module sits inside a declared outcome traversal rather
      than replacing one;
- [ ] if the module appears to decide next work, traversal closure,
      semantic target movement or graph-function identity, the boundary
      has been repriced under the graph-execution profile;
- [ ] the active boundary carries lifecycle confirmation against the
      canonical operational lifecycle chain of SPEC_METHOD §2, with each
      phase answered, declared not applicable with a reason, or recorded
      as a named `Gap:` or `Unanswered:` item; and
- [ ] release, deployment, live usage, telemetry and retirement claims are
      confirmed against product, requirement, design, release or
      operational authority rather than derived from implementation
      convention or fixtures.

For a new or materially changed boundary, the compact hard-gate version of
this checklist is (P6):

- [ ] accepted Ontology before promotion or closure and, where
      design-gated, before retained implementation establishes an
      unresolved or contradictory relation or chooses a materially
      non-equivalent network;
- [ ] complete entity lifecycle, authority and function-derivation
      evidence;
- [ ] whole-family Prime contraction, accepted atom domains, realisation
      projection mappings and declared composition and effect algebra;
- [ ] proportional capability and foundation selection for material
      generic mechanics and dependencies, with bounded discovery, frontier
      disposition, and exact role and authority conservation;
- [ ] pure functions in the semantic centre;
- [ ] immutable carriers with no shared mutable semantic state;
- [ ] one owner per truth surface;
- [ ] low coupling between admission, algebra and effect edges;
- [ ] no hidden runtime authority in semantic code;
- [ ] accepted domain, sequence and state-machine projections of the
      Ontology;
- [ ] complete cross-view axiom evaluation with no bypassed realisation
      gap;
- [ ] functional equivalence to specification and, when present, the
      reference realisation at the semantic boundary;
- [ ] lifecycle confirmation or named lifecycle gaps against the canonical
      operational lifecycle chain of SPEC_METHOD §2; and
- [ ] negative proof for imperative or open bypass.

The checklist is language-agnostic. It governs module design, carrier
design, data-entity design and review of realisation work in any language
(P1). For an unchanged boundary, the hard gate is the accepted basis plus
evidence of no material semantic-boundary delta; it does not require a new
Ontology, IACS, three-view asset, cross-view evaluation or unit-test lane
(P2; §7 Gate and retrospective work).

## 12. Adoption and relations

### Adoption

Who may adopt this profile is stated once in
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §7](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#7-collective-reference-frame-basis):
inclusion in the selected method cut makes the profile available, and only
Product authority adopts it. This profile adds no adopter. The adopting
Product's authority may record its adoption by citing the profile in ADRs
or design surfaces; naming it in the project's agent entry surface (such
as `AGENTS.md`) as the preferred realisation discipline; using it as
review criteria for implementation-migration tickets; and classifying
implementation modules by the taxonomy of §9 (P2, P6).

When the profile is adopted, the project applies it consistently across the
named boundary: Ontology and architecture derivation; design modules;
runtime or execution kernels; prompt assembly and reporting paths;
constructors and materialisers; and projection and query surfaces. For
migrations involving carrier closure, schema closure or governance
boundaries, projects should make the boundary closure evaluators (§3)
explicit in the governing ADR or ticket rather than leaving them implicit
(P6).

Every new or materially changed adopted semantic boundary declares or
cites its accepted Ontology before claiming design-method completion. The
Ontology evidence includes entity lifecycle, authority, function
derivation, whole-family Prime, each accepted atom's admitted domain,
atom-to-realisation projection mappings and projection traceability, at
the granularity applicable to the material change (P6, P2). When the
material change includes schema or typed carrier work, the project derives
and reconciles the IACS from that Ontology before claiming design-method
completion. When the new or materially changed boundary is derived from an
existing realisation, the project also publishes the reference-to-target
derivation asset and the Ontology-derived three-view design asset before
claiming design-method completion for the changed boundary. When the new or
materially changed boundary has active implementation, the project also
publishes a module-derived unit test lane (ASSURANCE §15) before claiming
closure for that change (P6).

Partial adoption is allowed, but the adopted boundary and adopted rule
family should be named explicitly. Partial adoption may narrow scope; it is
not used to claim design-method completion while skipping the evidence
needed to audit, refactor or reconstruct the realised boundary (P6, P2).

### Relationship to other members

SPEC_METHOD governs constitutional process, authority flow, repricing and
migration law; RELEASE governs release cut, Product, install,
qualification and version-line promotion evaluation; the graph-execution
profile ([ODD](ODD.md)) governs graph-native constructive carrier law; this
profile governs preferred realisation structure inside implementation and
design modules; the UX profile ([UX](UX.md)) refines this profile for UX
surfaces with rendering, state-transition and effect-membrane rules and is
loaded only when the work realises a UX surface (P6). So SPEC_METHOD answers what is
lawful process; RELEASE what is a lawful release, Product, install,
exact-cut acceptance and selector-promotion decision; the graph-execution
profile what is lawful graph-native product shape; this profile what is
the preferred implementation design discipline when you want
Ontology-first derivation, low coupling, no interface bleed, and explicit
authority and effect management; and the UX profile the additional
discipline that applies when a module realises a UI surface.

For products governed by the graph-execution profile, that profile decides
whether the operative unit is an outcome traversal, graph function, GTL
module or ABG runtime boundary; this profile then governs the
deterministic module structure that realises, evaluates, adapts or
projects inside that boundary (§2). When that boundary includes a UX
surface, the UX profile adds the render-purity, reducer-purity,
effect-membrane and AssetSurface-binding rules required for strong
functional consistency between front end and back end (P6).

The module lifecycle confirmation rule (ASSURANCE §16) detects whether the
realisation has enough lifecycle signal to be safely built and reviewed.
It does not decide release eligibility, exact-cut acceptance, selector
promotion, install policy or operational rollout; those remain governed by
RELEASE and project-owned release, deployment or operational surfaces
(P6).

### Identity defaults from a bound runtime realisation

A consumer-bound realisation of the ABG role under the graph-execution
profile may publish default identity generators, validators and
normalisers for its own runtime surfaces and for the default ODD surface
kinds used by default `F_D` helpers; the permission is scoped to that role
and does not extend to other runtime realisations (P3, P6). Their standing as
defaults and the identity law of their override, its preservation
conditions and its publication surface are
[IDENTITY §7](IDENTITY.md#7-default-formats-and-overrides).

The helper's F_D eligibility is the common §5 contract referenced in §2; an
identity default grants neither that eligibility nor additional writes.

### Non-goals

What this profile does not require (one specific programming language,
elimination of all imperative code, monadic or category-theory vocabulary,
replacing every exception with a custom algebraic type), what it does
require of implementation shape, and the composition and effect algebra
that remains required where a boundary composes higher-order or effectful
computation are stated once in
[SPEC_METHOD §2 Realisation shape](SPEC_METHOD.md#realisation-shape) (P1,
P4a).

# EVALUATION

Tier 1. Owns how claims are justified and accepted: claims, evidence,
independent assessment, review results, acceptance, conformance of
realisations and the equivalence ladder, the qualification of frames and
of the method itself, and actual-use evidence of adequate attention.
Consumes [FOUNDATIONS](FOUNDATIONS.md), whose
[Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results) own the core result values this member
uses; it defines no result values of its own.

## 1. Claims

A load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the
governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker
property it excludes, and its falsifier, before a witness is selected.
Without these it is evidence discovery, not proof. Packaging, syntax,
compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for a
semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claim because
the weaker property is easier to measure (P6).

Where a claim about a construction concerns its recursive or repeated
work, it is one of the four kinds the construction relation keeps apart,
preservation, progress, termination and outcome satisfaction
([ACTIVATION §1](ACTIVATION.md#construction-relation)), and states which.
Its witness is an assertion whose predicate is the full obligation, a
necessary condition of it or part of a sufficient conjunction, and the
claim states which. Its expected result has assertion provenance and its
execution has execution provenance, as
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Assertions and observation](FOUNDATIONS.md#assertions-and-observation)
and [Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
define them; a passing check of a necessary condition establishes that
condition and no more (P1, P6).

Boundary congruence. A checker, validator, harness, reviewer or other
assurance surface supporting promotion or closure binds the exact claimed
subject and its authoritative composition relation. Evidence over one file
or carrier proves only that boundary; it cannot establish a multi-file or
carrier-set claim. Cross-carrier satisfaction and conflict are decided at
the declared composite boundary (P3, P6). A claim of mechanical enforcement
names an executable or reproducible predicate and a witness reachable
through the declared ordinary assurance path; a planned or
specification-only harness is planned evidence, not observed verification,
and until both the predicate and such a witness are observed the claim
remains open or is explicitly downgraded to the planned property (P6).

A claim's quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed its evaluated
evidence. Generalising a local defect or observation needs a declared
inference relation, the relevant comparable population, explicit
counterexample treatment and governing evidence. Later counterevidence
invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is
superseded, withdrawn or requalified (P6). The quantifier rule and the
boundary rule are false if assurance observes a weaker or different
subject, if per-carrier evidence closes an unevaluated composite claim, if
mechanical enforcement lacks its predicate or a reachable witness, if
planned evidence is reported as observed verification, if a verdict outruns
its evaluated population or declared inference relation, or if dependent
verdicts survive material counterevidence without requalification.

### Foundation to law: claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance

This family, claims, evidence, assessment and acceptance (F6 in the index
of [FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law)),
decides when a claim is supported, how it is assessed and who accepts it.
It covers §1 to §5 of this member. Its instance premises are: (a) claims
about exact subjects are relied on for promotion, closure or release; (b)
the evidence available is finite, and may observe a weaker or different
subject, or another basis, than the one claimed; (c) a constructing actor
may be probabilistic or otherwise fallible; (d) each boundary at which a
claim is relied on has a decision owner. They are conditions of the work
this family governs, not commitments, and do not follow from finite
capacity alone.
P0's premise that a step's output is a candidate until evaluated is cited
by name. The standing of the consequences below is stated in
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).

| Premises, with standing | Consequence that follows | Rule in this member that states it | Added domain or policy choice, and its owner | Pillar |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| P6 (independent); instance premises a, b | By P6 evidence supports only the claim it is evidence for, and by (a) and (b) claims are relied on while the evidence is finite and may observe a weaker subject, so a load-bearing claim names its exact subject, the property claimed, the governing basis, the relation between witness and claim, the nearest weaker property it excludes and its falsifier before a witness is selected; without these it is evidence discovery, not proof. Packaging, syntax, compilation, presence, invocation or local behaviour never substitutes for a semantic, authority-bearing, installed, release or end-to-end claim because the weaker property is easier to measure | [§1](#1-claims), first paragraph | none | 9 |
| P3 (independent), P6 (independent); instance premise b | By P3 a claim binds its exact subject, and by (b) evidence may observe another subject, so an assurance surface supporting promotion or closure binds the exact claimed subject and its authoritative composition relation; by P6 evidence over one file or carrier proves only that boundary and cannot establish a multi-file or carrier-set claim, so cross-carrier satisfaction and conflict are decided at the declared composite boundary | [§1](#1-claims), Boundary congruence | each claim's composite boundary: the authority that declares the claimed subject and its composition relation | 2, 9 |
| P6 (independent); instance premise b | By P6 a claim holds only on observed evidence, and by (b) a plan is not an observation, so a claim of mechanical enforcement names an executable or reproducible predicate and a witness reachable through the declared ordinary assurance path; a planned or specification-only harness is planned evidence, not observed verification, and until both are observed the claim stays open or is downgraded to the planned property | [§1](#1-claims), Boundary congruence, the sentences on mechanical enforcement | the ordinary assurance path: the project's assurance design under [ASSURANCE](ASSURANCE.md#1-verification-layers) | 8, 9 |
| P6 (independent); instance premise b | By P6 a claim holds only as far as its evidence, and by (b) the evidence is finite, so a claim's quantifier, population and scope cannot exceed its evaluated evidence. Generalising a local defect or observation needs a declared inference relation, the comparable population, explicit counterexample treatment and governing evidence; later counterevidence invalidates every dependent verdict until the claim-evidence relation is superseded, withdrawn or requalified. The rules of §1 are false under the falsifiers §1 lists | [§1](#1-claims), the quantifier rule and its falsifiers | the inference relation and the comparable population of a generalisation: the author of the claim, who declares them with it | 9 |

The review-flow refinement applies P6's separation of operation, evidence and
decision to [Landing, closure and release](#landing-closure-and-release): making
a candidate available cannot establish its claims. P3 binds provisional use to
an exact subject, and P4b with ACTIVATION §7 preserves and invalidates dependent
results. Permitting authorized landing beside pending QA, and providing
[Declared Product acceptance gates](#declared-product-acceptance-gates), are
explicit domain policies of §5, not consequences of finite attention alone.
The concrete gate and its acceptance owner are Product selections. Consumers
are EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12's cadence, TICKETS §7's closure application and the
Project Reference-Frame Basis template. The exact report-effect refinement of

## 2. Separation

An unchanged-subject deterministic evaluation uses the operation profile of
[AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS §5](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#5-traversals-and-functor-kinds).
That owner's authority boundary applies; kind classification establishes no quality conclusion.
Authorized witness persistence and construction of the judged domain
subject remain separate. The total deterministic qualification is additional
to the evaluation profile, under the [migration relation](RELEASE.md#deterministic-kind-migration).

Three bases stay distinct (P6, P1): the semantic basis, the constitutional
and accepted-design relations that define what a claim means; the evidence
basis, the exact artifacts, events, logs, tests and observations used to
evaluate it; and the state projection, a current view derived from admitted
semantic and evidence bases. Semantic law defines what an evaluation means;
evidence supplies observations; the evaluator applies the declared
relation; decision authority disposes. One actor may lawfully perform
several; the record keeps them distinguishable. This section owns these
separations. [RF-007](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-007-semantic-evidence-and-verdict-separation)
binds them to a frame declaration and
[AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)
to an a_c model; each adds only its domain binding.

An evidence change can invalidate a verdict without any change of law.
Whether a given change does so is decided by the reuse rule of
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse), and where it
does, the invalidation is mandatory and takes effect before reliance. A
projection change can invalidate a view without changing semantic truth;
when a derived view is stale is decided by
[ACTIVATION §2, Staleness of derived surfaces](ACTIVATION.md#staleness-of-derived-surfaces).
A semantic change requires lawful re-entry and invalidates affected
downstream acceptance. A broad digest may conservatively
invalidate a review; it does not prove that every semantic relation
changed (P1, P6).

Structural conformance decides closed syntax, types, identities, references,
bases and mechanically decidable predicates. Semantic fidelity decides
meaning and materiality. Structural success is evidence for semantic
review, not a substitute for it. A checker decides the structural subset; it claims a
semantic or authority subset only under an exact lawful decision contract
supplied by the model. For a_c models,
[AC-018](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-018-structural-and-semantic-separation)
and [AC-019](AXIOMATIC_CALCULUS.md#ac-019-valid-model) bind this rule to
the model's records and validity conditions (P1, P6).
A valid parse, a valid map, a green test and a historical judgment each
establish exactly their own claim. Evidence bound to a basis other than
the evaluated one is excluded by basis; it is not admitted with a narrower
scope (P3;
[RF-005](REFERENCE_FRAME.md#rf-005-exact-basis-and-coordinates)).

## 3. Independent assessment

A constructor's self-review is construction output, not assessment. Where
promotion needs independent assessment, the assessor evaluates the exact
live subject, authority paths, proof and installed state, not the
constructor's summary (P6, and P0 with its premise that a step's output is
a candidate until evaluated; instance premise (c) of §1 Foundation to law).
This section decides what counts as independent assessment. Which
boundaries require it is a policy choice of the Spec Method, owned by
[TICKETS §7 Execution and verification authority separation](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007);
a governing basis may add boundaries.

Protocol: where method qualification applies
([§7 Method self-qualification](#method-self-qualification)), the subject is
frozen by identity before material reference exposure; elsewhere it is
stabilised by an immutable identity or an equivalent exact-subject relation
sufficient for the claimed assessment. The assessor records its
expectations from the governing source before opening the candidate; it
reads the subject at that identity or relation, never a mutable working
tree; it makes no repair; it does not assess its
own authorship. Reusing the constructor's judgment does not satisfy
independence; shared mechanical evidence may be reused, judgment may not
(ACTIVATION §7). Binding a returned assessment to its producer, subject,
basis and evidence authenticates the result; it establishes neither the
assertion provenance of its expected answer nor the execution provenance
of its run, which
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Parallel derivation and mutual assurance](FOUNDATIONS.md#parallel-derivation-and-mutual-assurance)
requires separately (P6, P3). Membership in a plan authenticates nothing,
an unauthenticated result satisfies no required assessment, and a result
bound to another subject satisfies no planned assessment
([FOUNDATIONS §4 Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results));
no cryptographic or transport protocol is prescribed for the binding (P6). Any post-exposure revision is a declared intervention: it
is either a method constituent with its own qualification boundary or a new
qualification subject, and it cannot retroactively make the original
frozen construction pass. This law prescribes no actor type or count,
review-round count, engine, prompt or orchestration (P6).

Author identity is the party responsible for the content of a realised
subject. It is distinct from actor identity, whoever performs one
operation, which is an identity and not an authority
([FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)).
Authorship is one of the conditions on
which the independence of an assessment rests; the evidence conditions are
the other (P6, P3).

Reporting a defect, supplying a counterexample or identifying behaviour
already required by governing law does not by itself author the realised
subject. Contributing wording, design or policy that is adopted into the
subject, including through directions for a particular repair, is authorship
of that contribution. A
reporter may assess a later repair only when the existing assessment grant,
authorship relation and evidence-independence conditions permit it; a
reporter gains no review authority from having found the defect. A person
who authored an adopted repair cannot supply its required independent
assessment by calling that authorship a finding (P6, P3).

Independence rests on authorship and on the evidence conditions above, not
on a new context. The assessor may read the same governing sources as the
constructor. A fresh context alone establishes no independence, and it
supplies no review authority the author lacks: an author that opens a
fresh context to review its own candidate is still its author, and its
review is self-review, which stays construction output and cannot be
relabelled as independent assessment (P6;
[TICKETS UP-007](TICKETS.md#execution-and-verification-authority-separation-up-007)). A contribution received from another author stays that
author's wherever it is carried, and that author's reading of it supplies
no independent acceptance of it (P6).

Independence across actor families is declared, not assumed. Whether two
activations of one model family are independent for a semantic judgment is a
policy the governing basis states for the claim; the default where it is not
stated is that they are not independent.

## 4. Review results

A review returns one core result
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results)) for each declared
predicate it evaluated, with: the exact subject and basis, the evidence
consulted, the findings ranked by consequence, each finding's evidence and
the smallest bounded correction, the residual uncertainty, and the
invalidation conditions. A declared predicate the review planned and did
not evaluate has no result (FOUNDATIONS §4, Results). The review names it
as not performed and reports no core value for it, neither
`indeterminate` nor `falsified`, so that conjunction keeps it apart from
an undecided predicate and from required coverage that no planned
assessment addresses
([FOUNDATIONS §4, Conjunction of results](FOUNDATIONS.md#conjunction-of-results);
P5, P6). It may recommend a disposition
([ACTIVATION §3](ACTIVATION.md#3-step-results-and-disposition)), which is
evidence only and never a disposition; it does not apply one. A finding
without evidence a consumer can chase is commentary.

### Result and triage projection

Where a review returns findings with technical triage, the triage is the
assessor's evidence-bound assessment of each finding against the exact
evaluated claim and basis. Severity, the assessor's grade of consequence,
is evaluation evidence. Priority, the effect on the current promotion
boundary and the disposition are the decision owner's (ACTIVATION §1,
Roles and delegation; when a finding can block is
[§5, When a finding blocks promotion](#when-a-finding-blocks-promotion))
and stay distinct values even where a
Product-defined policy maps one to another. A recommended disposition
is evidence for the decision owner: it is not a disposition, a
priority or a boundary effect, and it is never adopted mechanically (P6,
RF-007). The fields of a triage are declared by the profile that adopts it, and
the scales it uses are bound by the adopting Product (P2, P6).

The projection of the finding-level triage payload is total over the core
values of [FOUNDATIONS §4, Results](FOUNDATIONS.md#results). A predicate
not performed has no result and so no triage payload; the payload class
`indeterminate` never stands for it. The payload classes `complete`,
`indeterminate` and `not_applicable` classify the triage only; they are
not new results, dispositions, priorities or lifecycle states (P5, P1).

| Core result | Finding and triage payload | Decision-owner consumption constraint |
|---|---|---|
| satisfied | an explicit no-finding state; triage `not_applicable`; evidence, residuals and invalidation stay present | priority and boundary effect are `not_applicable` to this result unless another exact consumed result supplies a finding |
| falsified | one or more exact findings; triage `complete` where supported, keeping `indeterminate` fields where evidence cannot close them | apply the Product-owned priority and boundary policy without mapping severity mechanically to a disposition |
| indeterminate | a partial finding or observation state; triage `indeterminate`; the exact evidence gaps and residual uncertainty | keep the uncertainty or reactivate a capable evaluation; do not consume it as satisfaction or as a closed finding |
| out_of_frame | the evaluated claim needs an undeclared material relation or evaluator capability; triage `indeterminate`; the missing relation or capability and the exact reconfiguration pressure are named | refine or reconfigure a capable activation and keep the claim unresolved; do not consume the result as satisfaction or falsification |
| invalid_basis | a basis failure; triage `not_applicable`; invalidation evidence and basis-repair pressure | refuse to consume the result and return through the declared basis re-entry relation |

An adjacent observation outside the evaluated claim does not replace the
claim-relative result. The assessor returns it separately, with triage
`not_applicable` to that claim and the exact repricing or re-entry
pressure; the decision owner returns it to its declared owner without
creating a claim-relative block, or another review round, from its
severity alone (P6, P2).

The assessor returns to the decision owner, not to the constructor. It does
not edit the candidate, direct the repair or authorise continuation (P6,
§3).

Recording the assessment is a separate artifact effect. Where the activation
grants it, the assessor may write the exact named findings carrier under
[TICKETS §4 Review findings and bug items](TICKETS.md#review-findings-and-bug-items).
That grant adds no candidate-repair authority or acquisition route. A review
has covered its declared subject only when every planned predicate has been
evaluated or lawfully removed from that subject; a partial return preserves
the unperformed coverage. Closing the review activity does not satisfy a
falsified or unresolved work claim (P6, P5).

Purpose and material relation: every configuration keeps severity,
priority, boundary effect and disposition separate. The rule applies to any
assessor and decision owner; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md)
binds its Reviewer and Executive instance (P6).

## 5. Acceptance

Acceptance is the decision owner's disposition over an unchanged subject;
recording it cannot widen it, and it exhausts only the instance and interval
it names (P6, P2).
A work item closes by the condition it stated, not by a reviewer's approval;
a reviewer result is an input to closure, never the closure. Green labels,
document counts, review counts and historical outcomes are not acceptance.
A human decision may be exercised directly or through an explicitly admitted
bounded proxy. What a proxy grant names is
[IDENTITY §6](IDENTITY.md#6-authority-identity-and-conservation-stdo-up-004)'s,
and what a proxy can never decide is
[FOUNDATIONS §2 Authority kinds](FOUNDATIONS.md#authority-kinds)';
for acceptance, a change a proxy cannot make re-enters at its owning
relation ([ACTIVATION §1 Roles and delegation](ACTIVATION.md#roles-and-delegation)).

Where the subject is a successor, its acceptance evidence includes the
successor disposition record of [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
(STDO-UP-015), which states the law: the exact predecessor immutable cut
the successor evolves, and one semantic disposition for every predecessor
claim capable of affecting the successor. A claim whose disposition is
unresolved cannot be qualified and so cannot be accepted; how the record
is evaluated is [RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015).
An intentionally removed disposition is a decision of the current Product
authority, and its record is that decision (P6, P3, P4b).

### Landing, closure and release

Landing makes an exact candidate available at an authorized checkpoint or
integration destination. It is an operation under its existing grant, not
acceptance of the candidate's claims. Work closure applies the stated closing
condition; release applies the separately selected publication and acceptance
conditions of [RELEASE](RELEASE.md). Record these as separate decisions (P6,
P3).

Review supplies QA evidence for those decisions. A pending review does not by
itself hold landing: an admitted candidate may land after its bounded work
and fix pass, while review of that exact candidate runs beside subsequent
authorized work. A required review holds the closure or acceptance claim that
depends on its complete report. A governing landing condition, applicable hard
stop or missing operation authority still prevents landing; availability is
no waiver. [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §12](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#qa-cadence-and-repair-rechecks)
binds the optional profile's repair/recheck cadence (P6, P2).

Permitted downstream work may consume a landed candidate before its review
reports, carrying its exact identity, unresolved conditions and dependency
links. This is provisional use, not admitted truth. A later material finding
invalidates the affected dependent results under
[ACTIVATION §7](ACTIVATION.md#7-closed-result-and-reuse); unrelated valid results
remain reusable. Repair and re-evaluation follow those dependencies before
further reliance (P4b, P6).

### Declared Product acceptance gates

A Product-owned frame basis, or a work contract explicitly delegated that
choice by the basis, may declare a gated handoff between two Products. It
names both Product identities, the directed relation, exact candidate/claim,
required review and coverage, acceptance conditions and decision owner. Until
that review has covered its declared subject and the acceptance conditions
are satisfied, the downstream Product cannot accept the candidate as an
admitted input or close claims dependent on that acceptance. Authorized
provisional work and repair may continue under the preceding section (P6,
P2).

The gate's declaration is explicit; co-location, a dependency or this available
mechanism creates none. Existing user-acceptance, release/go-live and other
Product boundaries retain their own conditions. This member declares no
particular Product gate or extra capture-review hold on landing (P6).

### When a finding blocks promotion

A finding is a defect a review reports against the exact claim it
evaluated (§4). Blocking current promotion is the decision owner's act
over that finding (§4, Result and triage projection). This section is the
one statement of when a finding can block; profiles and work carriers
refer to it and add only their domain triggers.

A review verdict is bounded by the exact reviewed claim and its applicable
hard stops ([ACTIVATION §4](ACTIVATION.md#4-totality-and-refinement)). A
finding can block current promotion only when it:

1. falsifies that claim;
2. exposes competing or ambiguous authority on the claim's acceptance
   path;
3. violates applicable active authority, safety or retained accepted
   behaviour; or
4. establishes a material architectural decision with durable
   consequences that forecloses an admitted Product outcome.

These conditions are necessary. Which of them suffice is decided as
follows:

| Consumed condition | Effect on the current promotion boundary |
|---|---|
| a valid falsification of a mandatory claim governed by a non-waivable hard stop | the boundary blocks, whatever the assigned priority or the decision cutoff |
| any other finding meeting one of the four conditions | the decision owner decides blocking from the exact affected claim, the governed outcome or decision the work serves ([ACTIVATION §1, Intake](ACTIVATION.md#intake)), the applicable hard stops and the Product-owned cutoff policy; below that cutoff no block follows mechanically, and an accepted residual is retained explicitly |
| a finding meeting none of the four conditions | it does not block |
| an observation outside the exact reviewed claim | repricing or re-entry input, returned as §4 states: by itself it does not widen the reviewed subject, block its bounded claim, or require a new ticket, artifact, review round or implementation increment |

Severity selects neither priority nor a block mechanically, and priority
neither erases severity nor waives a hard stop. The decision cutoff is the
adopting Product's policy; this member sets no cutoff (P6, P2). This law
applies at any promotion boundary; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#promotion-constraint-projection)
binds the Executive instance. Purpose and material relation: one owner
gives every review consumer the same blocking condition. A bounded review
does not block on observations outside its claim, while a non-waivable hard
stop still blocks.

## 6. Conformance of realisations

A realisation aⱼ conforms to a specification Σ when its interpreted behaviour
satisfies Σ under a declared interpretation contract (P1) and an independent
judgment (P6). Several realisations may conform to one Σ; sufficiency does
not require unique derivation or equality with an incumbent. A weak Σ that
admits materially different behaviours either declares the latitude or is
repaired before a decision-complete design is claimed.

Equivalence ladder. The ladder is the list of the four claims named next,
each a rung; the rungs are listed, not ordered, and no rung implies
another. Conformance, semantic equivalence, computational equivalence and
categorical equivalence are separate claims with separate evidence (P1,
P6). Conformance establishes neither identical behaviour outside Σ nor
equal cost. Semantic equivalence of realisations claims that two
realisations, or a realisation and a declared reference outcome, have
identical interpreted behaviour on a stated domain, behaviour outside Σ
included. In this member semantic equivalence is always this equivalence
of realisations, not the equivalence of concepts across bounded contexts
that
[PRODUCT_DEFINITION §5](PRODUCT_DEFINITION.md#5-bounded-context-semantic-resolution)
governs, and semantic conformance, in the comparison rule below, is
conformance with the governing semantic basis as Σ. Computational
equivalence claims that two realisations compute the same function at
equal cost for declared workloads on a declared architecture H.
Categorical equivalence is a claim about categories and the maps between
them: FOUNDATIONS §4, Formal fragment, owns what a category or functor
claim must show and defines the symbols 𝒜, ℐ and 𝒞_H used here, and a
map's preservation of identities and composition is a further claim
distinct from every rung.
For a proposed span 𝒜 → ℐ and 𝒜 → 𝒞_H, conformance to Σ, semantic
equivalence and computational equivalence remain different claims.
A claim of categorical equivalence meets each item of the Formal fragment
that applies to it, as that section states them. This rung adds one
requirement of its own to those items: a quasi-inverse functor, and
natural isomorphisms between each composite of the functor with its
quasi-inverse and the identity functor, on a stated domain. An analogy or matching result
is insufficient. Evidence for one claim is not reported as a result for
another (§1). The ladder keeps a matching output, an analogy
or a passing conformance check from being read as equivalence or as
preserved structure (P1, P6).

Layered sufficiency. A specification arranged in layers is sufficient when
a competent actor can derive a conformant next layer from each layer; the
derivation need not be unique, since different realisations may satisfy the
same upper layer, and the test is sufficiency, not determinism. A failure
to derive at any boundary is a defect of the upper layer: unclear,
contradictory, underspecified, not concrete or decomposable enough, or
polluted with accidental lower-layer detail. A boundary that can be crossed
only by hiding a major unresolved ambiguity is not yet sufficient even if
some downstream artifact can be produced. For an already accepted relation,
reconstruction may reuse its exact current basis and sufficient evidence
after checking applicability and invalidation (ACTIVATION §7);
reconstructability requires a correct reconstruction route, not its
execution at every use, grants no restart authority and does not excuse
stale success. The claim determines the reconstruction span; a local
selected function does not require recreating the whole subject. New
material counterexamples still challenge the affected relation (P2, P1,
P0). [SPEC_METHOD §2 Reconstruction litmus](SPEC_METHOD.md#reconstruction-litmus)
applies this law to the method's own chain, with diagnosis per layer.

Comparison. After freeze the evaluator compares the frozen result against
the mandatory governing semantic basis for semantic conformance or
equivalence. A separately held expected or reference outcome, if one exists
and is applicable, is optional evidence and explicitly non-authoritative;
semantic equivalence to it is required only where the governing basis
requires it. A lawful alternative construction permitted by the basis
passes. Subjective similarity to the basis or the reference is insufficient
to establish conformance or equivalence. Byte or structural identity,
unique derivation, determinism and incumbent equality are not generic
comparison criteria. A construction outside the declared competence or
configuration envelope cannot indict generic method sufficiency (P6, P1).

For representation-benefit experiments, an optional design is to compare
equivalent substantive information and access while independently varying
relevant counterexamples retained, absent, or stale and out of scope.
Include the existing contract and the simplest adequate qualified plain-text
fix. State outcome oracles and the units and boundaries of acquisition,
rendering, reasoning, repair and assurance cost. Scale trials to the claim,
risk and resources; this guidance prescribes no universal trial count or
new review cycle (P2, P6).

Information-equivalent benefit can support an architecture decision;
retention benefit supports context-selection policy; stale-material failure
targets provenance and invalidation. No benefit or higher total cost supports
retaining the existing construction. Outcome correctness and unresolved
obligations remain visible. A Propose–Probe–Compose harness is one possible
experiment strategy, not a dependency or acceptance oracle. Consumer
adequacy remains distinct from functor laws under
[FOUNDATIONS §4 Formal fragment](FOUNDATIONS.md#4-algebra).

### Return of a reconstruction

A reconstruction return is the return of a task that builds or assesses
one member of a successor against its predecessor. It states under three
separate heads what it claims and the evidence for each, and claims none of
them by a byte or size measure. Semantic conservation: a disposed claim of
the predecessor keeps its meaning in the successor text, judged by reading
both texts against the disposition
([RELEASE §9](RELEASE.md#9-successor-baseline-conservation-stdo-up-015)
owns the dispositions and their conservation reading). Demonstrated
reduction: a deciding path of the successor costs less than the same path
in the predecessor on a declared measure, shown by the trace of both paths
with the declared tradeoffs. Mere relocation: text moved from one owner or
carrier to another without a change in meaning and without a traced
change in any deciding path. Relocation reported as reduction, or
conservation claimed from unchanged bytes, misreports the claim (§1, P1,
P6). The three heads stay separate in the return as the rungs of the
ladder do above; a frame for a reconstruction task binds this
distinction.

### Foundation to law: conformance, equivalence and qualification

This family, conformance, equivalence and qualification (F7 in the index of
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law)),
decides when a realisation, a frame or the method itself is shown fit for
what it claims. It covers §6 and §7 of this member and the
[CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md) member; a rule in CONFORMANCE is marked
"outside this member" in the third column. Its instance premises are: (a)
one specification may have several realisations; (b) realisations, frames
and the method are made by fallible constructors and relied on by actors
who did not make them; (c) qualification evidence comes from a finite set
of cases, run by actors inside declared envelopes. They are conditions of
the work this family governs, not commitments, and do not follow from
finite capacity alone. P0's actor-change premise, that the actor of one
step need not be the actor of the next and may re-acquire declared sources
but not private memory, is cited by name. The standing of the consequences
below is stated in
[FOUNDATIONS §3 Foundation to law](FOUNDATIONS.md#foundation-to-law).

Consumers of these rows, where an actor enters them (FOUNDATIONS §3

- Row 7, method self-qualification: [§3 Independent assessment](#3-independent-assessment), Protocol, where the subject is frozen by identity where method qualification applies; [EXECUTIVE_BASELINE §5 Exact candidate](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#exact-candidate), [§10](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#10-derived-reviewer-frame), [§12 step 4](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#4-executive-evaluates-the-work-result) and [step 5B](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#5b-candidate-requires-independent-review), [§17](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#17-actor-binding-and-independence), which adds this section's declared envelope, and [§18](EXECUTIVE_BASELINE.md#18-profile-qualification), which creates no second qualification process; [CONFORMANCE](CONFORMANCE.md#conformance), its preamble, whose assessments are by an independent assessor under this section.
